title: Check yourself: where did the request stop?

questions.stem: After a change, the IncomingListener in 50_server.xml writes to queue auth in the default Space, and 30_txnmgr.xml reads queue auth from the Space tspace:switch. Both files deploy without a warning. A terminal sends a purchase. What does the server's log show for it?

options.text: A receive by the channel and nothing after it, since no session reads the queue the Context went to
options.says: the listener and the TransactionManager meet only in a queue of one Space; with different Spaces the Context waits where no session reads and expires

options.text: A receive by the channel and nothing after it, since the listener drops a message no session has asked for
options.says: the listener never checks for a reader; it writes the Context to the queue and returns

options.text: A receive, a TransactionManager event and a send, since the shared queue name is what ties the two together
options.says: the queue name and the Space together are the link; the same name in another Space is another queue

options.text: A receive, a TransactionManager event and a send, since every Space name refers to the one default Space
options.says: tspace:switch is a Space of its own, separate from the default Space

origin.section: 1.2 The Listener and the TransactionManager Meet Only in a Queue

questions.stem: A new deployment script forgets to copy the jar that holds your participants into lib/. Q2 starts and lists 30_txnmgr.xml and 50_server.xml as deployed. What do you find in deploy/ and on port 8000?

options.text: 30_txnmgr.xml renamed with .BAD, and nothing on port 8000, since Q2 stops deploying after a failed file
options.says: the file could be read, so it keeps its name, and Q2 deploys the following files as usual

options.text: 30_txnmgr.xml renamed with .BAD, and the port accepting terminals, since each file is deployed on its own
options.says: only a file Q2 can't read or build is renamed; a failure inside init leaves the name and one warning

options.text: 30_txnmgr.xml under its own name, and nothing on port 8000, since Q2 stops deploying after a failed file
options.says: QBeanSupport logs the failure and Q2 carries on; QServer starts and listens

options.text: 30_txnmgr.xml under its own name, and the port accepting terminals, since each file is deployed on its own
options.says: the TransactionManager fails in init and logs one warning, the file keeps its name, and QServer starts and feeds a queue nobody reads

origin.section: 1.3.1 Spot the Problem: The Package Rename

questions.stem: A server's 00_logger.xml lists ProtectedLogListener first, protecting fields 2 and 35. Its 30_txnmgr.xml sets neither debug nor debug-context. A purchase with the test card 5555555555554444 is refused with 12. Where does log/q2.log show that card number in clear?

options.text: Nowhere in the file, since the masking listener runs before every writer
options.says: the listener masks only messages that are themselves in the event; the Context in the transaction event prints its messages unmasked

options.text: Nowhere in the file, since a refused purchase writes no transaction event
options.says: the TransactionManager writes an event for aborted transactions too, with the Context in it by default

options.text: In the transaction event, since the Context it holds prints its messages unmasked
options.says: debug-context defaults to debug, which defaults to true, and ProtectedLogListener doesn't look inside a Context

options.text: In the channel's receive, since the masking listener handles only the transaction event
options.says: the channel's receive holds the message itself, which the listener masks

origin.section: 1.6 The Transaction Trace Dumps What the Log Filter Can't Mask

questions.stem: Both TransactionManager sessions are stuck for a minute on a database that stopped answering. The IncomingListener's timeout is 15000. A terminal sends an echo and waits 30 seconds. What happens to the echo?

options.text: It expires unread after 15 seconds, since that is how long a Context may wait in the queue
options.says: the listener writes the Context with its timeout as the lifetime; no session takes it in time, so it expires and the terminal times out

options.text: It expires unread after 15 seconds, since the listener closes a connection that has waited that long
options.says: the timeout is the Context's lifetime in the queue; the listener doesn't touch the connection

options.text: It is answered once a session frees up, since the queue keeps each Context until a session takes it
options.says: the Context has a lifetime; after 15 seconds it is gone, long before a session frees up

options.text: It is answered once a session frees up, since an echo needs no participant that uses the database
options.says: every request, an echo included, waits in the same queue for a free session
